dissents.topic: Severity of the synthetic-key derivation change in sign_message_by_id / sign_message_by_address

positions.position: P0 spec-widening risk: the new RPC path applies convert_secret_key_to_synthetic to a key fetched by p2 puzzle hash, and no proof or pubkey-pinning test demonstrates the resulting pubkey matches the pre-refactor pubkey; possible double-synthesis.
Did not flag a correctness regression in the key-derivation change; treated the extraction as directionally sound and focused on duplicated dispatch, naming, layering, and tests.

dissents.topic: How verify_signature should handle unknown SigningMode

positions.position: sign_message silently defaults unknown modes to CHIP_0002 while verify_signature raises — the asymmetry is a latent bug; both should be exhaustive or raise.
The verify_signature else branch is dead/unreachable given the closed enum and should be removed or replaced with assert_never; defensive-as-substitute.
Gratuitous: a one-shot dataclass wrapping a 2-tuple of (pubkey, signature) that callers immediately unpack — return a tuple instead. BAD-TASTE.
Third pubkey/signature dataclass next to two existing response types; structure doesn't earn its keep — tuple was sufficient.
Did not flag the new dataclass as a problem.

dissents.topic: Whether the PR should be split

positions.position: THREE-PATCHES: extraction, per-wallet method removal, and new tests should be three reviewable/bisectable commits.
Did not raise diff-splitting as an issue.

issues.description: Specification silently widened: sign_message_by_id/by_address may double-apply synthetic key derivation with no proof pubkeys are unchanged
issues.detail: Original DIDWallet.sign_message and NFTWallet.sign_message took the inner p2 private key and applied calculate_synthetic_secret_key inside the wallet method. The new RPC code fetches a key via wallet_state_manager.get_private_key(await wallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash()) and then applies main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic to it. If the keystore-returned key already corresponds to the synthetic key for that p2 puzzle hash, the transform is applied twice. No invariant, proof, or pubkey-pinning test demonstrates the resulting public key equals the pre-refactor public key — the new tests only verify a signature against its own returned pubkey (tautological). TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum is a non-total function — silent fallthrough handles the fourth (is_hex, safe_mode) case implicitly
issues.detail: The free function enumerates three of the four (is_hex, safe_mode) combinations as if/elif and returns CHIP_0002 by an unguarded fallthrough for the remaining case. A 2x2 boolean input has four states; expressing only three explicitly and relying on 'and the rest must be the default' is exactly the kind of reasoning failure that produces wrong code when a future SigningMode is added. Should be a total function written as a 2x2 truth table (e.g., a dict keyed by (is_hex, safe_mode)) so coverage is self-evident. (Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, and Pike also flag this as P1 readability/correctness; Dijkstra raises severity to P0 on totality grounds.)

issues.description: Duplicated mode-to-message-bytes dispatch between sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: Both functions in chia/wallet/util/signing.py re-implement an if/elif ladder mapping SigningMode -> bytes-to-sign/verify, with subtle structural asymmetries (sign_message branches on CHIP_0002_HEX_INPUT then BLS_* then defaults to CHIP_0002; verify_signature groups {CHIP_0002, CHIP_0002_P2_DELEGATED_CONDITIONS} together and raises on default). The central invariant of a signing library — signed bytes equals verified bytes for every mode — should be enforced by construction via a single message_for_mode(mode, message) -> bytes helper, not by hand-maintained parallel ladders.

issues.description: sign_message silently defaults unknown SigningMode values to CHIP_0002 while verify_signature raises on unknown
issues.detail: sign_message's final else branch treats anything not matching the explicit modes as CHIP_0002 tree-hash encoding; verify_signature raises ValueError for unknown modes. A future SigningMode added without updating sign_message will silently produce a valid-looking but wrong signature instead of failing loudly. Both paths should be exhaustive (raise on unknown), or use a match statement so the type checker forces coverage.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists three times in the same module: free function + @property on two request classes
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a module-level signing_mode_enum(request) plus @property signing_mode_enum on SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID, each delegating to the free function. Same name across three definitions invites confusion, shadowing, and drift. Pick one shape — preferably a single helper signing_mode_for(is_hex, safe_mode) -> SigningMode keyed by the two booleans — so callers cannot reach the same answer via two contracts.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic placed on Wallet is a stateless function masquerading as an instance method
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(self, secret_key) does not touch self — it is calculate_synthetic_secret_key(secret_key, DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH). Callers reach it as self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...), implying per-wallet behavior that does not exist. Move it to chia/wallet/util/signing.py (or beside calculate_synthetic_secret_key) as a free function or @staticmethod. (Severity split: Knuth/Torvalds/Pike rate P2; Hickey/Liskov/Dijkstra rate P1.)

issues.description: Leaky abstraction: signing util does not centralize what it claims — callers still reassemble lookup + synthetic-key + sign at every site
issues.detail: sign_message_by_address and sign_message_by_id in wallet_rpc_api.py each perform get_private_key(puzzle_hash) -> convert_secret_key_to_synthetic -> sign_message. The signing library promised to encapsulate signing, but the synthetic-key derivation, keystore lookup, and puzzle-hash discovery all leak back into the RPC. A higher-level entry point like sign_message_for_puzzle_hash(wsm, puzzle_hash, message, mode) would place the contract 'given a puzzle hash, produce a CHIP-0002 signature' in one place.

issues.description: Spec missing: sign_message / verify_signature lack documented preconditions, postconditions, and error contract
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py is now the public boundary for signing but the contract is implicit: valid SigningMode values, per-mode message format (utf-8 vs hex string), what `address` means and when it is required, when ValueError is raised vs when VerifySignatureResponse carries error. verify_signature's docstring is also stale (still references :param request:). This is a security-sensitive surface; the spec needs to be written down with the same care the verifier expects from callers.

issues.description: LSP-shaped issue: current_p2_puzzle_hash gains incompatible signatures across DIDWallet and NFTWallet with no declared supertype contract
issues.detail: DIDWallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash() takes no args; NFTWallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash(nft) takes an NFTCoinInfo. They are de facto siblings in the WalletProtocol family but have incompatible signatures and no declared protocol method. A caller cannot substitute one for the other. State the contract on the protocol (or split into two clearly-named operations), or document explicitly that this is not polymorphic.

issues.description: Wrong layering: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types
issues.detail: The signing util now depends on an RPC wire DTO defined higher up the stack, while SignMessageResponse is defined locally as an internal dataclass. The boundary is inconsistent and contradicts the stated goal of making the util reusable from non-RPC code. Have verify_signature return a small internal result (tuple[bool, str | None] or local dataclass) and let the RPC layer adapt it into VerifySignatureResponse.

issues.description: Three patches submitted as one diff
issues.detail: The change does three reviewable things: (1) extract sign/verify into a shared util, (2) replace per-wallet sign_message with current_p2_puzzle_hash + RPC-side synthesis, (3) add tests for sign_message_by_id and sign_message_by_address. Each is bisectable on its own; together they are harder to read and harder to revert if one piece regresses. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: SignMessageResponse dataclass is gratuitous
issues.detail: A new module-private frozen dataclass with two fields (pubkey, signature) is introduced just to be unpacked at every call site into SignMessageByAddressResponse / SignMessageByIDResponse. The previous code returned tuple[G1Element, G2Element] which was fine. Adding a class for a 2-tuple of unrelated values is abstraction-for-its-own-sake. (Pike rates this P2.)

issues.description: signing_mode_enum property is recomputed multiple times per request — bind once
issues.detail: In sign_message_by_address and sign_message_by_id, request.signing_mode_enum is accessed three times per handler invocation, each access re-running the if/elif ladder. Bind to a local once at the top of the handler — cheaper and documents that all sites refer to the same mode. (Knuth rates this P2.)

issues.description: Dead else branch in verify_signature: 'Unsupported signing mode' is unreachable
issues.detail: verify_signature enumerates the four SigningMode members and then raises 'Unsupported signing mode' in an else. Because SigningMode is a closed enum and signing_mode_enum coerces or raises beforehand, the else is unreachable. DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE for correctness. Either remove the else (and replace with assert_never to assert exhaustiveness to the type checker) or document the precondition that would make it fire.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_nft_id is tautological — verifies signature against its own returned pubkey
issues.detail: The test calls AugSchemeMPL.verify(response.pubkey, expected_message_bytes, response.signature). Any well-formed (pubkey, signature) pair from sign_message will satisfy this regardless of which key was used. It does not pin response.pubkey to the expected synthetic-of-inner-p2 key, does not cross-check against pre-refactor behavior, and does not exercise verify_signature with address binding. To meaningfully constrain behavior, derive the expected synthetic pubkey from the NFT's inner p2 puzzle hash in the test and assert equality; also run through verify_signature with the NFT's p2 address. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address discards the verify_signature result
issues.detail: The new test calls rpc_client.verify_signature(...) but does not bind or assert on the return. VerifySignatureResponse carries isValid: bool and an optional error; an invalid signature would return a response object, not raise, and the test would pass. Add `assert res.isValid is True` and ideally assert on absence of error. (Torvalds rates P2; Dijkstra rates P1.)

issues.description: DID-path of sign_message_by_id remains untested
issues.detail: PR adds a test for sign_message_by_id on the NFT path. The DID branch of sign_message_by_id in wallet_rpc_api.py was also refactored (current_p2_puzzle_hash, synthetic-key conversion via main_wallet, get_coin) and is not covered. Add a DID-path test to lock the contract on the other subtype before further refactors.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring still references a 'request' parameter that no longer exists
issues.detail: The function was lifted from an RPC handler taking a single request object; the docstring still reads ':param request: :return:' even though it now takes five keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address). Either drop the docstring or rewrite it to document each parameter and the address-binding semantics (CHIP_0002_P2_DELEGATED_CONDITIONS uses the raw pubkey puzzle; other modes use the synthetic-key puzzle hash).

issues.description: Variable named hex_message holds non-hex bytes in three of four branches
issues.detail: Inside sign_message the local is named hex_message but holds a tree hash (CHIP_0002 path), a utf-8 byte string (BLS_MESSAGE_AUGMENTATION_UTF8_INPUT), or hex-decoded bytes. Name encodes a false invariant. Rename to message_to_sign to mirror verify_signature's message_to_verify so the symmetry between the two halves of the scheme is obvious.

issues.description: Error message rewording without justification: 'Invalid inner DID puzzle.' -> 'Invalid DID inner puzzle.'
issues.detail: DIDWallet's error string was reworded with no semantic change; current_p2_puzzle_hash also introduces a new 'Missing DID inner puzzle.' alongside 'Invalid DID inner puzzle.' Drive-by prose edit in a refactor PR — either revert the wording or leave it; don't churn error messages in unrelated refactors.

issues.description: Test asserts BLS verification manually but does not assert signing_mode in the response
issues.detail: test_sign_message_by_nft_id verifies the BLS signature directly but does not assert that response.signing_mode reflects the requested (is_hex, safe_mode) combination. A one-line assert per case (`assert response.signing_mode == SigningMode.X.value`) would lock in the truth table signing_mode_enum encodes and catch any future regression in the fall-through case.

issues.description: Tests duplicate the implementation's mode-to-bytes ladder
issues.detail: test_sign_message_by_nft_id manually constructs Program.to((CHIP_0002_SIGN_MESSAGE_PREFIX, message)).get_tree_hash() and bytes(message, 'utf-8') etc. inline for each mode — the same ladder as in signing.py. The natural test is to call the just-shipped verify_signature() with each mode; otherwise the test is a parallel reimplementation that will pass even if both sides drift together.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor is directionally right — pulling sign/verify into chia/wallet/util/signing.py and replacing per-wallet sign_message methods with current_p2_puzzle_hash + a shared signing function is cleaner — but five of six reviewers find the extraction was mechanical rather than fully decomposed. Strongest convergent findings: (1) signing_mode_enum is non-total with a silent CHIP_0002 fallthrough over the (is_hex, safe_mode) 2x2 (flagged by all six), and the symbol is duplicated three times in the same module; (2) the mode-to-message-bytes dispatch is replicated as parallel if/elif ladders in sign_message and verify_signature with subtle asymmetries (sign defaults silently to CHIP_0002, verify raises) that a single message_for_mode helper would eliminate; (3) convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is a stateless function placed on Wallet and reached through main_wallet, mis-suggesting per-wallet behavior. The strongest preserved disagreement is Dijkstra alone calling the diff REFUSED on a P0 spec-widening concern: the new RPC code applies convert_secret_key_to_synthetic to a key fetched by p2 puzzle hash, and no test pins the resulting pubkey to the pre-refactor pubkey — the new NFT test only verifies a signature against its own returned pubkey (tautological) — while the other five reviewers treat this as acceptable extraction. Test quality is also broadly criticized: test_sign_message_by_address discards the verify_signature result, the DID path of sign_message_by_id is untested, and the NFT test reimplements the same dispatch ladder it should be exercising via verify_signature.
